label: prop:brunnian-binding-channel
title: The binding multiplier is the unsigned coordination count, not a Gauss linking number: forced by Brunnian topology and bar-parity
html:
Proposition. Let a nuclear composite be assembled from component knots whose pairwise inter-component linking pattern is Brunnian — every pairwise Gauss linking number vanishes, as for the Borromean carrier \mathrm{L6a4} of {}^3\mathrm{He}/{}^4\mathrm{He}. Then the mutual binding contribution to the crossing energy is carried entirely by the sign-blind coordination-count channel, and the signed linking-number channel is identically zero. Consequently the binding multiplier is an unsigned coordination count, complementary in bar-parity to the bar-even mass self-trace, and can never coincide with it.

Setup

Write the mutual (inter-component) crossing energy of a component pair with n_+ positive and n_- negative crossings in the Skein-signed form n_+ q - n_- q^{-1}. The proved decomposition of crossing energy splits it into two channels:

  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-)(q + q^{-1})}_{\text{signed (strong, }\cosh\text{) channel}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q - q^{-1})}_{\text{unsigned (Coulomb, }\sinh\text{) channel}} .

The signed multiplicity is the writhe n_+ - n_- = 2\,\mathrm{lk}, the Gauss linking number; the unsigned multiplicity is the crossing count n_+ + n_-, a coordination count.

The Brunnian channel

A Brunnian pair has vanishing pairwise linking number, \mathrm{lk} = 0, i.e. n_+ = n_-. The signed channel then vanishes and the entire mutual/binding energy is the unsigned count channel; for a crossing pair at a substrate modulus q > 1 this channel is strictly positive. So the binding energy is nonzero even where the pairwise linking number is zero — the coordination count, not the Gauss linking number, is the correct binding carrier for a Brunnian nuclear link. A minimal Brunnian bond (n_+ = n_- = 1, the pairwise pattern inside \mathrm{L6a4}) contributes exactly one coordination unit, so a fully coordinated cluster carries \binom{A}{2} units and per-nucleon z = A - 1; which pairs bond is the coordination-graph question, saturation-limited for heavy A (the complete graph is excluded there, QOU.Mass.CoordinationSaturation).

The deuteron sits at the boundary. What coincides there is the two multiplicities — the writhe n_+ - n_- = 2\,\mathrm{lk} and the crossing count n_+ + n_-, which are what play the role of the binding multiplier — not the channel values, whose \cosh and \sinh weights differ at every q. The two multiplicities agree exactly on all-positive carriers, n_- = 0, and the positive Hopf link is such a carrier (n_+ = 2, n_- = 0, giving |\mathrm{lk}| = 1 and coordination z = 1, both multiplicities equal to 2). On a Brunnian carrier n_+ = n_- instead, collapsing the signed multiplicity to 0 while the unsigned one is the full crossing count. So the two invariants agree for a Hopf-bonded pair and diverge from A \geq 3, where only the unsigned count is non-vanishing.

Why the assignment is forced — bar-parity

Under the bar-involution q \mapsto q^{-1} the count (binding) channel is bar-odd, while the mass self-trace \mathrm{lw} = \tfrac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda \vdash c+1} \dim_q \lambda is bar-even — every quantum dimension satisfies \dim_q = \dim_{q^{-1}} (for the fundamental [2]_q = q + q^{-1}). A nonzero bar-even function is never bar-odd, so a binding multiplier and a mass multiplier occupy complementary bar-parity sectors and can never be the same object. This is the same \cosh/\sinh split the framework uses for the bar-even meson scale and its bar-odd Q_\beta partner. The assignment mass \leftrightarrow self-trace, binding \leftrightarrow coordination count is therefore a parity fact, not a modelling choice.

Scope

The channel structure, the Brunnian reduction, the coordination-unit map for minimal bonds, and the bar-parity orthogonality are proved (QOU.Mass.BrunnianBindingChannel, sorry-free). The two further residuals are now also settled. The mass \leftrightarrow self, binding \leftrightarrow mutual assignment is a theorem of the crossing partition plus the mass-deficit definition of binding (B = \sum_i m_i^{\text{isolated}} - m^{\text{assembly}} = -(\text{mutual energy}); the self energies cancel), so binding is exactly the inter-component pairing (QOU.Mass.SelfMutualPartition, sorry-free); and the crossing-count \to coordination coefficient is \tfrac{1}{2}\lvert\text{inter-crossings}\rvert in general, giving \binom{A}{2} units and per-nucleon z = A-1 for a complete graph of minimal single clasps. This is the discrete counterpart of the unsigned-invariant resolution reached independently on the electromagnetic-linking side. The additive partition lifts to the mass observable — whose self carrier is the multiplicative q-dimension Markov self-trace \mathrm{lw} — through the archimedean functor \tau = \log: a multiplicative amplitude has an additive free energy E = \log T, so the mass-deficit binding equals the connected (interaction) free energy -\log I, which is positive exactly when the assembly amplitude is suppressed (QOU.Mass.ArchimedeanTraceBridge, sorry-free).

Two multiplicative structures must be kept apart here, and an earlier version of this paragraph conflated them. For the normalised Jones polynomial the connected sum is exactly multiplicative, J(K_1 \# K_2) = J(K_1)\,J(K_2), whereas the disjoint union carries the loop value, J(K_1 \sqcup K_2) = \delta\,J(K_1)\,J(K_2) with \delta = [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. The matrix result that is actually proved — the Kronecker-product multiplicativity of the trace (QOU.MathlibExt.MarkovTraceMultiplicative) — models the disjoint union, not the connected sum. Consequently a genuinely independent assembly has I = \delta, not I = 1: adding an unlinked component costs \log \delta \approx 0.699 of free energy at the proton pin, and a Markov closure of an n-strand braid is normalised by \delta^{\,n-1}. The additivity therefore holds only up to that loop factor, which is exactly what QOU.Mass.ClosureNormalisationDefect makes precise (freeEnergy_closureNorm_additive_iff: additivity holds iff \delta = 1, excluded for q > 1). Two modelling inputs remain named rather than derived: that the substrate assembly amplitude is the Markov trace (a citable Jones theorem, carried as a hypothesis), and the dimensional dressing \mathfrak{m} = \mathfrak{m}_e\,\mathrm{Vol}\,\mathrm{lw}/\hbar_q^2 (CAL-1 scale, geometric volume, CAL-2 cusp) — calibration and geometry, not a fit. The exact saturated fraction B/A/\mathfrak{m}_N \approx \hbar_q^2 is a numerical coincidence, not a prediction: the empirical B/A peaks at 0.954\,\hbar_q^2 near A \approx 60 and falls, and the fundamental volume coefficient is a_V/\mathfrak{m}_N \approx 1.71\,\hbar_q^2.
